notes: What makes a USE procedure 'applicable' (answered once here; it is the question every SR of this shape in VII, VIII and IX asks). SR2's relative clause binds the procedure to the FILE: 'a file which is not in sequential access mode and for which an applicable USE ... procedure is not specified'. GR5 a-e say when a procedure applies to a file: one naming it, or one whose mode the file is open in. So at compile time a procedure is applicable to the file when it names the file or names a mode the file CAN be open in. The refuter's narrower reading (only a procedure that can run for the invalid key condition, i.e. ON file or ON I-O for a DELETE) rests on IX.1.3.5 GR3, a general rule about what happens at run time; the syntax rule does not say 'for the invalid key condition', and a USE ON INPUT does run for this very DELETE when the file is open INPUT (status 49; probe u-in-in). A program that reaches an invalid key with no procedure associated violates GR3's 'must', whose result is undefined (§1985:I.1.6), not a compile-time obligation. The text leaves 'applicable' undefined, so the precedence applies: GnuCOBOL 3.2 enforces no such requirement at all, and IBM Enterprise COBOL and Micro Focus have no compile-time requirement either; the least restrictive static reading the text supports is therefore the file reading, which is also how CCVS-85 SQ148A is written (READ with no AT END covered only by USE ... OUTPUT). Under that reading INPUT, OUTPUT and I-O conform for an indexed random or dynamic file, but EXTEND does NOT: such a file can never be open EXTEND (IX.4.4.3 SR1), so a USE ON EXTEND procedure can never apply to it, and HasApplicableUse counts it (d-useEXT and u-ext-io: compile, run, status 23 handled by nothing). That is PB5413's EXTEND arm, and this answer agrees with PB5413's reading; PB5413 should also claim this row. The row is therefore PARTIAL: the phrase, access-mode scope, file-named, I-O, INPUT, OUTPUT, GLOBAL and other-file arms are right; the EXTEND arm under-rejects. kb/Work PB5413 holds the defect (adjudication: held-85/set6/decisions.json).

next.reason: §1985:IX.4.3.3 SR2: 'The INVALID KEY phrase must be specified for a DELETE statement which references a file which is not in sequential access mode and for which an applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure is not specified' (indexed file). 2023 has no such syntax rule (§2023:14.9.10.3 SR2 only forbids the phrase in sequential access mode); §2023:14.9.10.4 GR11 makes the transfer of control depend 'on the presence or absence of the optional INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY phrases in the DELETE RECORD statement as specified in 9.1.14', and the refused case is stated by §2023:9.1.14 GR4: 'If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified in the input-output statement and there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement'; so too §2023:9.1.14 GR3: 'If control is returned from those statements or there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement'. Words that differ: 1985 'must be specified'; 2023 'not specified ... there are no applicable ... exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end'. A statement 1985 refuses is accepted by 2023 with a stated run-time effect: a lifted refusal, so CHANGED (kb/Work PB5021), not REMOVED.
